PullRequest.Title: Retain full Codex shell output across chat reloads
PullRequest.Body:

Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/338051
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/328596
Follow-up to: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335016

- Keep Codex command output up to 80,000 UTF-16 code units inline, using a Codex-owned character limit.
- Retain larger output in the owning chat's session database within the existing 10 MiB UTF-8 limit. Show the first 400 characters unchanged with **Open Full Output (Read-Only)**, without keeping a terminal alive.
- Wait for storage before publishing ordinary or recovered command completions. Preserve per-chat signal order, keep full inline output if storage fails, and suppress queued publication after disposal.
- Preserve tool-call identity across live events and replay. Coalesce sandbox pre-flights only when raw command invocations match, including shell flags. Unwrap Bash/zsh and PowerShell/pwsh scripts for display and existing script inspection, not identity.
- Restore retained resources on initial history reads and incremental refreshes, even when native replay output is short, empty, or null.
- Share the recovery eligibility check between retention and completion mapping. Remove retained output when rollback or revert removes its turn; session deletion removes the remaining database.
- Leave subagent output, unretained output, and output above 10 MiB unchanged. Reject obviously oversized strings before UTF-8 allocation and check exact byte size for multibyte output.

This is a Codex Agent Host adapter change. It does not change AHP, Copilot/Claude retention, workbench rendering, or approval policy.

### Validation

Verified at `2d31e1fb172d3017b660ed1bfe4e399df4558124`:

- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- Focused Codex suites — **307 passing**:

  ```sh
  npm run test-node -- --runGlob '**/agentHost/test/node/codex/{codexPrewarmEviction,codexMapAppServerEvents,codexReplayMapper,codexShellCommand,codexTerminalOutput,codexChatDiscovery,codexCreateChat}.test.js'
  ```

- `./node_modules/.bin/eslint $(git diff --name-only c364cc986a3..HEAD -- '*.ts')` — passed.
- `git diff --check c364cc986a3..HEAD` — passed.

Regression coverage includes delayed/rejected writes, missing turn rows, disposal, recovered completions, ASCII/UTF-8 size boundaries, raw PowerShell identity, rollback cleanup, and short or missing native history output. Failure, size-guard, identity, and restore regressions were observed failing against the preceding implementation before passing with the fixes.

The PowerShell identity and shorter-history cases use synthetic protocol payloads; they do not claim a captured reproduction from the pinned Codex runtime. Live manual verification of this head is pending. GitHub currently reports a conflict with `main`; these review fixes intentionally do not include an upstream merge.

### Manual verification

In a Codex Agent Host chat, ask the agent to run this exact shell command:

```sh
node -e "process.stdout.write('FULL_OUTPUT_BEGIN\n' + 'x'.repeat(131072) + '\nFULL_OUTPUT_MIDDLE\n' + 'y'.repeat(131072) + '\nFULL_OUTPUT_END\n')"
```

Verify:

- The card starts with `FULL_OUTPUT_BEGIN`, shows the raw 400-character prefix and truncation indicator, and offers **Open Full Output (Read-Only)**.
- The read-only editor contains the beginning, middle, and end markers.
- Closing and reopening the editor, then restarting the Agent Host and reloading the window, still opens the full retained output.
- Short output, such as `node -e "console.log('short output')"`, remains inline without a truncation indicator or full-output action.

On Windows or where PowerShell is available, repeat with:

```powershell
$x = 'x' * 131072; $y = 'y' * 131072; [Console]::Out.Write("FULL_OUTPUT_BEGIN`n$x`nFULL_OUTPUT_MIDDLE`n$y`nFULL_OUTPUT_END`n")
```

Verify that the card shows the script rather than the PowerShell wrapper, with the same retention and restore behavior.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- Write-before-publication and fallback behavior follow [`CopilotAgentSession`'s stored shell output capture](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/2d31e1fb172d3017b660ed1bfe4e399df4558124/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L5965-L5982).
- Restore-by-tool-call-id follows [`_restoreStoredShellOutputsForChat`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/2d31e1fb172d3017b660ed1bfe4e399df4558124/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L3745-L3771).
- Serving completed output without a live terminal uses the existing [`AgentService._resolveRetainedTerminalState`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/2d31e1fb172d3017b660ed1bfe4e399df4558124/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L5834-L5898).
- Storage ownership, turn-row requirements, and the 10 MiB limit come from [`SessionDatabase.storeTerminalOutput`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/2d31e1fb172d3017b660ed1bfe4e399df4558124/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/sessionDatabase.ts#L918-L937).

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path is direct from `_getChatMessages` and incremental `_refreshChatHistory`, both await `_restoreRetainedCommandOutputs` before publishing turns. `SessionDatabase.readTerminalOutput` performs SQLite reads of the full blob, retained output is explicitly bounded only at 10 MiB, and the new tests exercise retained commands whose native replay output is short, empty, and null. Only prevalence of that replay discrepancy is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: SQLite BLOB bytes, Uint8Array buffers, and decoded UTF-16 strings up to 10 MiB per retained command
Findings.PerformanceScaling: O(K * B) bytes read and decoded, where K is the number of retained commands with replay output <=80,000 characters and B is each retained blob size up to 10 MiB; the awaited loop also serializes their latency.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased chat-history latency and CPU/GC pressure from full-blob reads and decoding
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, Codex replay mapped the app-server's output directly and did not read or decode any terminal-output blobs from the session database during history loading.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: History restoration now loads the entire retained terminal-output blob from SQLite and UTF-8-decodes it when Codex replay supplies short, empty, or null output, then discards everything after the 400-character preview.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added restoration branch at RIGHT line 6756 calls `readTerminalOutput` whenever a retained command's replayed output is at most 80,000 characters; the next added line decodes the returned blob, while `codexRetainedCommandOutputContent` keeps only a 400-character slice.
Findings.Title: Read only the retained preview during history restore
Findings.Impact: Opening or refreshing a chat containing retained commands whose native replay output became short or missing can allocate and decode up to 10 MiB per command before any history is shown, increasing reload latency and causing avoidable memory/GC pressure. Multiple affected commands scale the total bytes read and decoded linearly.
Findings.Evidence: `_restoreRetainedCommandOutputs` runs on the chat-history critical path. For every retained command with replay output <=80,000 characters it awaits `database.object.readTerminalOutput`, whose implementation selects the full `output` BLOB after a size query, then `VSBuffer.wrap(storedOutput).toString()` allocates a full decoded string. The only consumer, `codexRetainedCommandOutputContent`, immediately slices that string to 400 UTF-16 code units. Retained blobs may be as large as `MAX_TERMINAL_OUTPUT_BYTES` (10 MiB per the PR contract), and the loop repeats serially for every affected command.
Findings.Recommendation: Add a bounded database read for just the preview prefix (or persist the 400-character preview alongside the retained blob) and use that here, while retaining the existence check needed to distinguish retained commands. Do not materialize the complete blob merely to construct the preview.

Scenarios.Scenario: Live completion of a parent Codex shell command with large output
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For output over 80,000 UTF-16 units and at most 10 MiB UTF-8, UTF-8 encoding and the SQLite write must complete before the command completion and every subsequently ordered chat signal are published. Non-qualifying and subagent output stays on the prior synchronous publication path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Encode up to 10 MiB of output and insert/update the terminal_outputs SQLite row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One database write per qualifying completed parent command; zero for output <=80,000 characters, over 10 MiB, storage failures before write, or subagent output.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The complete command output was published inline immediately and no session-database terminal-output write occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The write is newly awaited before publishing the matching completion, and subsequent signals queue behind it to preserve order.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of qualifying large command completions and each output's UTF-8 size, bounded at 10 MiB per command.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each SQLite database serializes terminal-output mutations through its turn-data sequencer. Notifications can start multiple retention promises, but writes execute serially; chat publication is also serialized per session by `_pendingChatProgress`.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No output cache is consulted before retention. The session database reference may already be warm, but each qualifying tool call gets its own write; tool-call IDs provide replacement semantics rather than coalescing. Failed writes fall back to the already-held full inline output.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff directly encodes the full string, starts a sequenced database mutation, and gates signal publication on its promise.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Local SQLite write duration and the frequency of multiple large outputs in one turn vary; the synchronous encoding and ordering dependency are certain. The intentional persistence-before-publication tradeoff and bounded 10 MiB size make this insufficient for a separate finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: The new persistence and ordering cost is intentional and bounded per command. Potential queued allocations were considered, but no separate high-confidence regression beyond the reported restore allocation was established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial chat reload and incremental watched-history refresh
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Codex thread history IPC completes first, then `_getChatMessages` and `_refreshChatHistory` await all retained-output restoration before returning or publishing turns. Full retained blobs are therefore read and decoded on the visible history-load critical path when replay output is short or missing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the Codex thread and full turn pages from the app-server process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One `thread/read` plus one or more paginated `thread/turns/list` IPC requests based on history page count; this history boundary already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same app-server history requests were required before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Supplies all turns before mapping and remains on the history-load critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover retained outputs and reconstruct terminal preview content from the per-chat SQLite database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One filesystem stat/open attempt when at least one rendered command exists, one SQLite size query per rendered/coalesced shell command, and for each retained command with replay output <=80,000 characters an additional full-output read that internally performs a size query plus a BLOB query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Replay mapped app-server output directly and performed no session-database access for command output.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All checks and reads are awaited before initial history returns or changed history publishes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective number of rendered shell calls after sandbox pre-flight coalescing; full-read cost further scales with the count and byte size of retained outputs whose native replay output is short, empty, or null.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cold-session reads are globally limited by `_coldSessionReadLimiter`; Codex history pages and retained-output checks run serially. Within restoration, commands are iterated sequentially, and SessionDatabase also sequences terminal-output reads.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The database may benefit from an already-open handle and OS/SQLite page cache, but there is no retained-ID cache or bulk lookup. Every replayed rendered command is checked again; incremental refresh limits this to commands in changed turns.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: both history entry points await the loop, the database implementation selects the full BLOB, and only a 400-character preview survives.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of commands with divergent short/null native replay output is runtime-dependent, but tests explicitly support that state. Blob size is concretely bounded at 10 MiB, so prevalence affects severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: full retained blobs are loaded and decoded solely to derive a 400-character preview, causing O(K * B) I/O/allocation on the history critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rollback or revert of turns containing shell commands
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing Codex `thread/revert` or `thread/rollback` IPC must complete first. The new database cleanup is then awaited before truncateChat returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Revert paginated history or roll back a number of turns in the Codex app server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One Codex app-server revert/rollback request per truncation, unchanged from before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single rollback/revert request occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authoritatively changes provider history and remains the primary required boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Delete terminal_outputs rows for reverted command IDs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One filesystem stat/open plus one SQLite DELETE per command item in all removed turns, including commands with no retained row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Rollback returned after the provider request and did not touch the session database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: New cleanup is awaited after successful provider rollback, extending truncate completion linearly with removed command count.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total commandExecution items across all removed turns, not merely the subset with retained output.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The code creates deletion promises for all command IDs with `Promise.all`, but SessionDatabase serializes each mutation through its turn-data sequencer, so effective database concurrency is one.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No retained-output membership cache is used. Cleanup safely no-ops when the chat database is absent; session deletion later removes the whole database.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: every removed command ID creates a distinct mutation, and the database sequencer makes them execute serially despite Promise.all.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large multi-turn reverts can contain many commands, but truncation is infrequent and each indexed delete is small. This was considered as boundary fan-out but not reported without stronger evidence of user-visible magnitude.
Scenarios.Verdict: The new cleanup has linear database fan-out, but on an infrequent workflow with small indexed deletes; evidence does not justify an additional performance finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Live/replayed shell identity preservation and PowerShell display unwrapping
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Raw shell identity comparison and wrapper unwrapping occur while mapping live/replayed command items before actions or turns are emitted.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of command items and command-string length after effective pre-flight coalescing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous and single-threaded per event/replay pass.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior changes; mapping is pure in-memory work over replay items and live mapper state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed mapping code only performs string/Map/array operations and reuses existing replay traversal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Command strings and replay item counts vary, but the added regex/display processing remains linear and no catastrophic pattern or boundary work was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression; the work is bounded in-memory mapping and does not add retained lifetime or expensive boundaries.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and all diff pages. One medium-severity serialization/allocation regression was submitted for reading and decoding complete retained blobs merely to reconstruct 400-character history previews. Live storage ordering, replay lookup fan-out, rollback cleanup, signal serialization, cache behavior, and lifecycle cleanup were also traced; no other candidate met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
